answers.core: Even if it proves possible to extend the AnimationNode system to implement this purely in script, the functionality would likely benefit from the performance and tight-integration of being in core. The AnimationTree editor will likely require special-case handling for 'external' animation nodes to make working with them as seamless as possible, and the functionality they would provide seems broad, useful, and non-intrusive on the existing animation system, at least from what my preliminary implementation of the feature has shown.
answers.workaround: There is currently no way to introduce this kind of hot-swapable animation tree concept in a way which could be considered sufficently flexible for the user cases outlined unless the hotswappable graphs were contained exclusively in the top-level node as a unique resource for each instance. This is simply too limited to be practically useful at scale.
